title: console-starter's two remaining hand-maintained lists still stand in for the real graph: Tailwind `@source` (18 of 29 aliases) and unprovided peerDependencies
body:
Out-of-scope finding from #3528 (PR closing that card: the vite alias table now covers its own import closure, pinned by `examples/console-starter/test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts`). Two *other* hand-maintained lists in the same example still describe the graph by hand, which is the class #3528 was about. Neither breaks anything a user hits today, so: `finding`, not queued.

## 1. `src/index.css`'s `@source` list is a second copy of the alias table

`examples/console-starter/vite.config.ts` now aliases **29** `@object-ui/*` packages to `packages/*/src`. `examples/console-starter/src/index.css` `@source`-scans **18** of them. Tailwind v4 only generates utilities it finds in a scanned file, so any utility class used *only* inside an aliased-but-unscanned package is silently absent from the stylesheet.

Measured over the 11-package gap, almost all of it is correctly scoped — `core`, `types`, `i18n`, `permissions`, `data-objectstack`, `mobile`, `providers`, `plugin-editor`, `react-runtime`, `sdui-parser` contribute **0** lines carrying Tailwind utility tokens. The exception:

| Package | Aliased | `@source`-scanned | Lines with Tailwind utility tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@object-ui/collaboration` | yes | **no** | 15 |

`@object-ui/collaboration` is UI-bearing and unscanned. This predates #3528 (it was already aliased before that fix), so it is not a regression from it.

The general point is the drift generator, not the one package: the `@source` list has to be edited by hand every time the alias table grows, nothing checks that it was, and the failure mode is missing CSS rather than an error. A closure check like the one #3528 added is possible here too — scan the aliased packages for utility tokens and require an `@source` entry for any that has them.

## 2. peerDependencies of the example's own dependencies are not provided by the example

`@object-ui/plugin-list` and `@object-ui/plugin-detail` are direct `dependencies` of the example and declare these `@object-ui/*` **peerDependencies** (`workspace:^`), which the example does not itself declare:

- `@object-ui/core`
- `@object-ui/fields`
- `@object-ui/permissions`
- `@object-ui/react`
- `@object-ui/types`

(`@object-ui/mobile` was in this list too; #3528's PR declares it, for exactly this reason.)

A peer means "the host provides this". In-monorepo, pnpm's `auto-install-peers` and the fact that other declared dependencies happen to pull the same packages in make it invisible. A fork consuming published packages under a strict-peers install is the case where it would surface. Worth deciding once whether the example's manifest should satisfy the peers of what it depends on, and whether the same holds for `apps/console` and `examples/byo-backend-console`.

## Verification notes

- Alias vs `@source` diff and the token counts were measured at `c29ceffb8` plus the #3528 branch; commands are in that PR's description.
- Duplicate search before filing: `is:open console-starter tailwind source` returned only #4065 (root `postcss.config.mjs`, unrelated); `is:open peerDependencies example declare` returned nothing.
